The pure class interface. 
public abstract class Aggregate<A>
  implements Formattable
The abstract superclass of all aggregate classes. It provides methods with default implementations for traversing the contents of an aggregate.

Version: $Id: Aggregate.pizza,v 1.1.1.1 1998/09/01 10:51:10 wg Exp $

reduce

public <B> B reduce(B z,
                    (B, A) -> B f);
Reduce elements of aggregate. 
 
  AGG{x1, x2, ..., xn}.reduce(z, f) = f(...f(f(z,x1), x2)..., xn)
Reduction order is determined by enumeration order.

reduceWithPos

public <B> B reduceWithPos(B z,
                           (B, int, A) -> B f);
Reduce elements of aggregates, passing the position of the reduced element. 
 
  AGG{x1, x2, ..., xn}.reduceWithPos(z, f) = 
        f(...f(f(z,0, x1), 1, x2)..., n-1, xn)
Reduction order is determined by enumeration order.

fold

public A fold((A, A) -> A f)
  throws NoSuchElementException;
Fold elements of aggregate. 
 
  AGG{x1, x2, ..., xn}.fold(f) = f(...f(x1, x2)..., xn)
  AGG{x1}.fold(f) = x1
Folding order is determined by enumeration order. @throws NoSuchElementException if aggregate is empty

equals

public boolean equals(Object other);
Equality of aggregates according to their enumerated elements. Two aggregates are equal, if their elements in order as enumerated are equal. Specializations of aggregates which don't care about the order (such as sets) may refine the notion of equality.

public int hashCode();
Hashcode of aggregates, defined as a sum of some of its elements. This hashcode function is compatible with the generic equality on aggregates, based on their enumeration.

hashCode in class Object

compare

public int compare((A, A) -> int ecompare,
                   Aggregate<A> other);
Lexicographical ordering of aggregates according to their enumerated elements. Produces a total order, provided the element ordering is total. Note, however, that this total ordering does not necessarily coincides with semantic equality. This is only the case if 
 x === y ==> x.enumerate() === y.enumerate()

See also:

compact

public void compact();
Compact this aggregate. This method has no semantic effect, but for some aggregate implementations it frees auxiliary memory allocated for the internal representation.
